attributes.name: aria-valuenow
attributes.values: position of the splitter, as the size of the primary pane

attributes.name: aria-valuemin
attributes.values: position at the smallest primary pane, usually 0

attributes.name: aria-valuemax
attributes.values: position at the largest primary pane, usually 100

attributes.name: aria-labelledby

attributes.name: aria-orientation
attributes.values: vertical for a splitter between side-by-side panes
attributes.note: Not on the pattern page. WAI-ARIA 1.2 defaults separator to horizontal, so a vertical splitter must say so.

rtlDecisions.question: In RTL, does ArrowLeft move a vertical splitter left on screen, or shrink the primary pane?
rtlDecisions.apg: Physical wording: Left Arrow moves a vertical splitter to the left. Silent on RTL. aria-valuenow tracks the primary pane size.

libraries.behaviour: The separator of Splitter has no arrow-key handler; only its collapse buttons are focusable. Pointer deltas are reversed for a horizontal splitter in RTL.
No splitter. Table column resizing reverses the horizontal delta in RTL so that the divider follows the arrow.

rtlDecisions.reason: The APG binding is physical and a divider is a physical object: it must go where the arrow points. The primary pane is at inline-start, so in RTL ArrowLeft grows it and raises aria-valuenow.

data.notes: Terminology trap: a "vertical splitter" is a vertical line between side-by-side panes, moved with the horizontal arrows. RTL: the page words the arrows physically and we keep them physical (rtl: visual): ArrowLeft always moves the divider left. The primary pane is the inline-start pane, on the right in RTL, so there ArrowLeft enlarges it and raises aria-valuenow, while in LTR ArrowLeft lowers it. Home and End are defined by pane size, not side, and do not change. A test must therefore assert the value change with the sign flipped in RTL and the pixel movement unchanged. No library studied implements arrow keys on a splitter (Ant Design's separator is pointer-only), so this decision is ours.
